name: Spillman Ranch
title: Spillman Ranch Window Cleaning | Bee Cave TX | CleanzATX
description: Window cleaning for Spillman Ranch Loop homes by the Falconhead golf course. Pure water glass from $10 a window, sprinkler spots out, stone soft washed.
intro: Spillman Ranch is the stretch of Falconhead along Spillman Ranch Loop, close to the golf course in Bee Cave. CleanzATX washes windows here, treats overspray spotting, and soft washes limestone and stucco.

sections.h2: What Spillman Ranch homes are like
paragraphs: Spillman Ranch Loop curves along the edge of the Falconhead course, and the homes that line it are priced from roughly $600,000 to $1.1 million. It is a small section of Falconhead, so the Falconhead HOA applies and the streets are open. Owners here chose the location for the green space, and many back walls look straight onto turf and mature trees. Walls are a mix of stucco and Hill Country limestone, with covered back patios that frame the golf views.
Window sets follow that idea: a wide back wall of glass, smaller panes on the street side, and a few tall entry windows up front.

sections.h2: What Spillman Ranch windows deal with
paragraphs: Next to a course, the water that waters the grass also waters your glass. Overspray from irrigation leaves hard water spots, usually in a fan pattern across the lowest panes. They are easy to ignore for a season and hard to remove after three. We treat them at $10 per pane, and our filtered rinse keeps new spots from forming while we work.

Turf also brings fine dust and clippings, and the open sightline means wind carries pollen onto the back wall in spring. Cedar pollen from December to February arrives first, followed by live oak. Stucco and limestone on a golf side wall collect a green cast in the shade, and the 12V soft wash lifts it without scarring the stone.

We handle Spillman Ranch with the other Falconhead sections, so a visit here usually sits on the same day as a few neighbors. If your back patio is covered and shaded, we mention that when we set up so furniture and cushions are moved out of the spray area. Patios and pool decks are cleaned by hand so they stay dry enough to use after. For many owners the practical bundle is exterior windows, screens and a soft wash of the back wall.

A 3,000 square foot house works out to about $300 for the exterior glass. Plan on roughly two and a quarter to three hours on site. If you want the interior hand cleaned as well, it comes to around $450 and adds about an hour and a half.

why: Golf course irrigation spots on back glass are something we treat regularly.
Stone and stucco on the course side get a gentle soft wash.
Covered patio and pool deck areas are cleaned by hand, so nothing floods.
We fold this loop into one Falconhead route for steady, predictable visits.

faq.q: What causes the fan shaped spots on my glass?
faq.a: That pattern comes from sprinkler overspray. Hard water in the irrigation dries into mineral spots. They can be removed, and the longer they sit the more they bond to the glass.

faq.q: Should I move my patio furniture?
faq.a: It helps. We keep water off cushions and fabrics where possible, but clearing the area near the back wall makes setup quicker and keeps everything dry.

faq.q: Do you clean outdoor living areas as well?
faq.a: Yes. Patios and pool decks are cleaned by hand so they do not get soaked, and flatwork like driveways uses a surface cleaner at $0.18 per square foot for concrete.

faq.q: Are you familiar with Falconhead HOA rules?
faq.a: We work throughout Falconhead and keep to normal daytime hours. If your HOA has a specific request, tell us when you text and we follow it.

faq.q: What is the price for a typical home?
faq.a: Exterior windows run $10 each or about $0.10 per square foot of home, so a 3,000 square foot house is near $300. The minimum job is $200.
